shots.title: Define terminal rollover eligibility and tracked audit record shape (#586)

hazards.description: The first audit bound the prior state but not the complete next state, accepted permissively normalized state, and could strand recovery after roadmap drift. Independent review required a full transition integrity payload, strict evidence shape, and audit-as-commit recovery semantics.

shots.notes: The final tracked audit records actor/request, exact prior and canonical next state, roadmap digest, dependency evidence, validated scorecard paths/digests, claims/session policy, and durable lineage.

shots.title: Implement slope sprint rollover --from --to with dependency and terminal-state checks (#586)

hazards.description: Roadmap-complete metadata initially allowed a forced unfinished source to satisfy a dependency on itself. Completion evidence now excludes the local source unless its exact gate-derived state is terminal.

shots.notes: The command selects the next authored dependency-eligible pending sprint, supports explicit forced/reasoned incomplete handoff, writes audit before replacement under locks, and reuses the exact audited next state after a crash.

shots.title: Teach sprint begin to emit the exact safe rollover recovery command (#586)

hazards.description: Fixing begin/start alone left older workflow rebind, review-tier initialization, PR guard, and portable-resume paths able to erase or ignore lineage. Retry rendering also needed platform-aware shell quoting and identity/pointer flag preservation.

shots.notes: Every normal cross-sprint entry now refuses destructive replacement, emits bounded eligibility-aware guidance, preserves meaningful retry flags, and verifies existing lineage before progressing.

shots.title: Cover terminal, dependency-blocked, in-progress forced, and audit-preservation rollover paths (#586)
shots.notes: Coverage includes terminal/forced/dependency/terminal-status matrices, 435/43.5 identity, corrupt state, audit tampering, next-state integrity, roadmap drift recovery, scorecard durability, duplicate flags, missing lineage, guard behavior, portable resume, and evolved target state.

conditions.description: Sprint state is consumed by commands, workflow synchronization, guards, portable recovery, claims, and PR gates, so a safe new transition required auditing and closing older mutation paths rather than adding one isolated command.

training.description: An audit is useful only when every downstream consumer verifies its lineage.
training.outcome: Begin, start, workflow synchronization, review-tier initialization, portable resume, agent guidance, and PR guards now preserve or verify rollover evidence.

training.description: Audit persistence is the transition commit point.
training.outcome: Crash recovery trusts the integrity-bound audit and tolerates later roadmap byte drift while reusing the exact recorded next state.

training.description: Missing and corrupt state are different operational facts.
training.outcome: Strict load and initialize/mutate helpers fail closed and preserve corrupt bytes.

training.description: Copyable recovery output is part of the security boundary.
training.outcome: Duplicate flags are rejected, output is bounded, and user values are platform-aware shell-quoted with actor and pointer flags retained.

nutrition.description: The final focused matrix passed 208 tests across rollover, state, workflow, begin/start, guards, agent output, review-tier initialization, and portable resume.
The complete repository suite passed 3,918 tests with 25 skipped after final review hardening and closeout evidence edits.
Production build and TypeScript typecheck passed, including packages/pi-extension.
Both independent lanes rejected multiple rounds, all required fixes were addressed, and both reviewers approved the final normal-flow lifecycle contract.

nineteenth_hole.how_did_it_feel: The command itself was straightforward; the real work was finding every older path that could silently make its audit meaningless.
nineteenth_hole.advice_for_next_player: Treat tracked lineage as a system-wide invariant and test recovery after evidence changes, not only the happy transition.
nineteenth_hole.what_surprised_you: A safe retry message had both identity correctness and shell-execution consequences.
nineteenth_hole.excited_about_next: S232 can now dogfood both modular roadmap sources and the audited S231-to-S232 handoff.

bunker_locations: Do not let roadmap-complete metadata satisfy a dependency on locally unfinished forced work.
Bind the complete canonical transition, then permit only documented target-state evolution.
Validate and digest evidence artifacts; identifiers alone are not durable completion proof.
Treat missing, corrupt, and valid state as distinct cases at every mutation boundary.
Audit every legacy overwrite path, including workflow resync, guards, and portable recovery.
Shell-quote copyable guidance and preserve actor, pointer, phase, and force semantics.
yardage_book_updates: src/cli/sprint-rollover.ts owns pure eligibility, contained evidence loading, integrity-bound audit persistence, crash recovery, and lineage verification.
src/cli/sprint-state.ts provides strict missing/corrupt/valid loading plus locked initialize, mutation, conditional phase update, and replacement primitives.
Sprint begin/start, workflow synchronization, completion guards, review-tier initialization, and portable resume no longer silently replace cross-sprint state.
Roadmap terminal dispositions are centralized and legacy encoded sprint identity is used for eligibility and labels.
course_management_notes: All implementation and review-repair commits are pushed; no PR merge is implied.
Independent architecture and adversarial reviewers approved the final implementation with tracked evidence.
slope sprint reset remains an explicitly destructive emergency exception and is no longer recommended for normal sprint handoff.
